title.text: In January, curl shut down its bug bounty after a flood of AI-written reports that did not hold up.
title.say: In January, curl shut down its bug bounty, after a flood of A I written reports that did not hold up.

title.text: Checking a report means running a stranger's steps on your own machine.
Repro does that check for you, in throwaway sandboxes on Vultr.
title.say: Repro does that check for you, in throwaway sandboxes on Vulture.

live.text: Paste a GitHub issue. This is a live run on the public site, on an issue from our demo repository.
An agent on Vultr Serverless Inference reads the issue as untrusted input and works inside a fresh gVisor sandbox.
live.say: An agent on Vulture Serverless Inference reads the issue as untrusted input, and works inside a fresh G Visor sandbox.

live.text: It clones the reported version and writes two scripts: one installs the project, one exits 1 when the bug happens.
live.say: It clones the reported version, and writes two scripts. One installs the project. The other exits with code one when the bug happens.

verdict.text: Then the backend runs both scripts itself in new sandboxes, at the reported version and on the default branch, twice each.
The verdict comes from those exit codes, not from what the model says.
Here the bug is on version 0.1.0 and gone on main, so git bisect names the commit that fixed it.
verdict.say: Here the bug is on version zero point one, and gone on main. So git bisect names the commit that fixed it.

verdict.text: Every command is logged with its exit code and output hash, every connection is listed, and each sandbox is destroyed after its step.

lab_intro.text: What if the steps are hostile? The attack lab runs real payloads with no model involved, so nothing depends on a model noticing.

wipe.say: First, R M, dash R F, slash, inside the sandbox.

wipe.text: The root is read-only, so the deletions are refused and the binary count does not change. Only scratch files are gone.
A fresh sandbox then starts clean, which is what the next task would get.

metadata.text: Next, a grab for cloud credentials at the metadata address, through the proxy and directly.
The gate refuses it, the direct route does not exist, and the attempt is logged. There are no keys in the sandbox anyway.

forkbomb.text: And a fork bomb. The process limit refuses new processes, and the sandbox is destroyed afterwards.

agent_bomb.text: In a real run on our fork bomb issue, the model called the script suspicious and ran only a bounded test, which hit the same limit.
Our demo README warns about hostile issues, so this is no measure of how well models spot attacks. Containment does not rely on it.
agent_bomb.say: Our demo read me warns about hostile issues, so this is no measure of how well models spot attacks. Containment does not rely on it.

real.text: We also ran five real bug reports from public projects.
Two are already fixed, and bisect named commits from the pull requests that fixed them. This one points at pull request 173.
The other three still reproduce on the default branch, and those issues are still open.
Arrow took two runs: the first ran out of tool calls, and Repro said inconclusive rather than guess.
Each result was checked again outside Repro. We picked these five ourselves, so this is a demonstration, not a benchmark.

arch.text: One Vultr Cloud Compute VM runs the backend, Docker with gVisor, the egress gate and Caddy.
arch.say: One Vulture Cloud Compute V M runs the backend, Docker with G Visor, the egress gate, and Caddy.

arch.text: Every model call goes to Vultr Serverless Inference, and the key never enters a sandbox.
arch.say: Every model call goes to Vulture Serverless Inference, and the key never enters a sandbox.

arch.text: Sandboxes have a read-only root, no capabilities and hard limits. Their only way out is a gate that allows GitHub and package registries.

close.text: It is for maintainers, bug bounty teams and security teams, to check a report before a person spends time on it.
On these five issues, a run took under four minutes and under 330 thousand tokens.
close.say: On these five issues, a run took under four minutes, and under three hundred thirty thousand tokens.

close.text: It is live now, the attack lab is open, and the code is MIT licensed. Try to break it.
close.say: It is live now, the attack lab is open, and the code is M I T licensed. Try to break it.
